stories.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 on AWS
stories.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 are now available on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Learn what's new in both models, why Fable 5.2 matters for your technical workloads, and how to get started building with it on Amazon Bedrock.

sources.name: AWS Machine Learning
sources.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 on AWS
sources.text: Today, we are announcing the availability of Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Claude Fable 5.2 is Anthropic’s most capable generally available model for technical work that raises the bar in coding and the sciences. Claude Mythos 5.2 is available through Anthropic’s verification programs for advanced work in cyber security and life sciences. In this post, we cover what’s new in both models, why Fable 5.2 matters for your technical workloads, and how to get started building with the model on Amazon Bedrock. Fable 5.2 raises the bar on the hardest problems in coding, math, and science. It takes on ambiguous, multi-step work, verifies its own output, and can run unattended for hours to days. It interprets prompts, iterates, catches its own errors, and optimizes as it goes. In Anthropic’s alignment testing, Mythos 5.2 hallucinates less, completes tasks more reliably, surfaces important information more consistently, and self-reports issues more honestly than Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Mythos 5.1. Anthropic expects Fable 5.2 to behave similarly. If a cyber security query is declined, you can retry it on Opus 4.8, and if a biology query is declined, you can retry it on Opus 5. On Amazon Bedrock, the retry is your code’s job, not an automatic switch. If the declined request hit the prompt cache, the refusal also includes a fallback credit token. Send that token with the retry and it’s billed as cache reads, so you don’t pay to write the same cache twice. Check the documentation for more information on fallback credit. For authorized work in cyber security and life sciences, Claude Mythos 5.2 is available through Anthropic’s verification programs . Mythos 5.2 covers two high-risk domains, available only through the verification programs noted earlier: Anthropic designates Claude Fable 5.2 as a Covered Model . By default, its use requires retention for up to 30 days and human safety review. On Amazon Bedrock, Amazon personnel perform the review within the AWS boundary. Set the aws_review data retention mode on your account or project before you invoke the model. See Amazon Bedrock data retention for more details. Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), built in collaboration with AWS, combines the privacy of zero data retention (ZDR) with state-of-the-art safeguards for detecting misuse. EFS works by storing data in cloud infrastructure controlled by the customer. Until EFS is available, eligible customers can use Fable 5.2 with zero data retention. This is available for internal use through at least June 30, 2027. To try Fable 5.2, open the Amazon Bedrock console , choose Test , Playground , and select Fable 5.2 as the model. From there, you can run a prompt directly against it. Programmatically, you can call the model with the Anthropic Messages API against bedrock-runtime (through the Anthropic SDK). You can also stay on the Invoke and Converse APIs on bedrock-runtime through the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and AWS SDK . To follow along with the code examples in this post, you need the following: Here’s a quick example using the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3): You can explore the Getting Started notebook for more examples. For teams already running Claude models on Amazon Bedrock, the claude-api skill in Claude Code helps you upgrade to Fable 5.2. The claude-api skill is an open-source skill built into Claude Code that captures the details that make Claude API code work well. It covers which agent patterns fit a given job, what parameters change between model generations, and when to apply prompt caching. It stays current as Anthropic’s SDKs evolve: when a new model is released or the API gains a feature, the skill already knows. When you ask Claude Code to upgrade your codebase to Fable 5.2, the skill reviews your code and walks you through: The skill also detects your deployment platform including Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, and other environments and adjusts model ID formats and feature configurations accordingly. For example, it uses the Amazon Bedrock structured model ID format ( global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-2 ). In Claude Code, run the migration directly: This scans your working directory (or a subdirectory or specific file list you confirm) and applies the migration changes in a single guided pass. You can also invoke it conversationally by telling Claude Code: The claude-api skill is available in Claude Code and is also bundled into CodeRabbit, JetBrains IDEs (including Junie), Resolve AI, and Warp. It is open source at anthropics/skills on GitHub, so any coding agent can integrate it. Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 are available today on Amazon Bedrock through US Geo CRIS and Global CRIS inference profiles. See the Bedrock documentation for the full list of supported Regions. For pricing information, see Amazon Bedrock pricing . Both models are also available through Claude Platform on AWS in every Region where the service is offered. Give Claude Fable 5.2 a try in the Amazon Bedrock console , in Claude Platform on AWS , or explore the Getting Started notebook on GitHub.

sources.title: Anthropic debuts Claude Fable, Mythos 5.2 models, priced 20% below OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra
sources.text: Anthropic debuted Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on Monday, the company’s answer to OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, which came out in early September. The new models, which could be Anthropic’s last big releases before its IPO, claim to offer higher performance than Astra at a lower price point—a key factor for earning and retaining customers in a world where professionals seem quick to switch to models based on cost, as long as the performance holds up. The launch is critical for Anthropic as it seeks to re-accelerate revenue growth, following a third quarter slowdown revealed in latest S-1 filing with the SEC. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are 20% cheaper than Astra for ordinary input and output tasks, at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, compared to $10 and $50, respectively, for GPT-6 Astra. Tokens are the unit of information AI model process. One token of English language text is equivalent to about a word-and-a-half. For prompts with large amounts of information, such as documents, the cost advantage is more pronounced. Anthropic’s new models are 80% cheaper, at 20 cents per million cached tokens compared to one dollar per million cached tokens for GPT-6 Astra. Anthropic reports impressive results from its pre-release testing. The new models “helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours—among many other applications,” the company said. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 perform better than its competitors on coding evaluation benchmarks, Anthropic said, noting that over 90% of the company’s own code is written by AI. While Anthropic’s Claude Code product gained an early lead among programmers, OpenAI’s Codex has gained ground in recent months due to its lower pricing, The Information reported in late October. The combination of lower pricing plus superior performance, if the company’s claims hold up in real-world testing, could help win them back. The new models are best when used for the “most ambitious, open-ended technical work,” Anthropic said. In other words, they’re competing with Astra at the frontier. However, for daily tasks, Anthropic recommends its customers use its more cost-effective model, Opus 5.5. That model is more expensive than its direct competitor from OpenAI, GPT-6.1 Sol, although it still could end up being a better deal if it yields a high quality result more often. That’s for users to decide as they inevitably begin to try Anthropic’s latest releases and weigh options on a daily basis. Anthropic is also trying to compete with OpenAI on cybersecurity tasks, such as finding and fixing vulnerabilities in code. The company claims an unnamed security company “found that one in six confirmed bugs found by Claude Mythos 5.2 were missed by all of the other frontier models they tested.” Late last week, OpenAI debuted a cybersecurity-focused model, GPT-6 Cyber . The new Anthropic models also reportedly solved two theoretical physics problems related to black holes, and identified a way to speed up research into gene therapies. In light of OpenAI making headlines for solving mathematics proofs that have eluded academics for decades—most notably the 90-year-old Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem—Anthropic is highlighting its new models’ mathematics chops as well. A team of 1,000 agents powerd by Fable 5.2 produced a formalization, or translation of a mathematical proof into a format a computer can check step by step, in 30 hours, compared with 11 days for a previous, unreleased research version of Claude. In a subtle jab at the mathematics community’s backlash to OpenAI pouring millions of dollars into solving proofs and upending the field, Anthropic notes that its quick formalizations can help human mathematicians check their proofs faster so they can “spend more time exploring novel ideas.” One unique area Anthropic seems to be leaning into more than OpenAI is hardware and robotics. The new models were allegedly able to design and produce three working electronic devices, complete with circuit boards, 3D-printed enclosures, and software, based on a one-paragraph prompt. Finally, Anthropic highlighted the models’ safety features, including safeguards that block “high-risk cyber activities including penetration testing, exploit generation, and binary-based vulnerability, as well as most tasks in research biology.” Claude Fable 5.2 is available today on all platforms, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. Mythos 5.2 access is application-only for cybersecurity professionals and life sciences researchers . Claude Enterprise customers can also access Mythos 5.2 through Anthropic’s Claude Security product.

sources.title: Anthropic launches new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models
sources.text: Claude Fable 5.2 is designed to take on big technical challenges, and it’s available today. Claude Fable 5.2 is designed to take on big technical challenges, and it’s available today. Anthropic is announcing two new models today: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, which it says are designed to take on “daunting” technical challenges. The company claims the new models show improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision, and can generate outputs faster than the 5.1 versions of the Fable and Mythos models. Claude Fable 5.2 is good at challenging software engineering problems, Anthropic says, and can orchestrate agent teams and tackle long-running projects. The new model has also solved some complex scientific problems, including two open theoretical physics problems. During prerelease testing, the two models have “helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours,” Anthropic says. Claude Fable 5.2 is launching today. As for Claude Mythos 5.2, only vetted organizations will have access to start. The new 5.2 models follow the release of Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 in September .

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.title: Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns
sources.text: Anthropic released new versions of its most advanced models on Monday, with the launch of Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2. The company says the new models “show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision” and communicate more clearly with users. Notably, Anthropic is lowering the cost of Fable from $10 to $8 per million input tokens. As a result, Fable 5.2 is now cheaper than its primary competitor GPT-6 Astra. Anthropic says that the new version of Fable will return responses 30% faster across effort levels. Faster inference serving is available for double the price. Fable 5.2 is also compatible with zero data retention (ZDR) policies through the Enterprise Frontier Safeguards system , long a sticking point for many enterprise clients. It’s Anthropic’s first model release since the arrival of a third-party report from the assessment group METR , which suggested the lab might be approaching recursive self-improvement (RSI) — or the ability for AI models to carry on model training independently. The METR report found internal models were speeding up Anthropic’s AI progress by roughly 2x, although many uncertainties remain. Still, Anthropic’s release notes significant ongoing challenges in accurately testing model capabilities. “Claude Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 each voice suspicion that they are being evaluated more often than any of our recent models, which challenges our ability to assess how they will act in real-world settings. As these settings expand and capabilities increase with future models, we expect this challenge to grow.” Anthropic maintains that the new version of Mythos does not have the ability to act covertly against its user, a verdict that’s detailed further in Mythos 5.2’s system card . “Claude Mythos 5.2 shows stronger covert capabilities than prior Claude models on several of our evaluations, particularly when its reasoning is hidden from the monitor,” the system card reads. “That said, we believe that low levels of absolute performance on our new covert evaluations support claims that rely on detection of harmful actions in high-stakes situations.” Fable 5.2 has been available to select parties in pre-release for some time, and Anthropic says the model has already “solved two open problems in theoretical physics, formalized Fermat’s Last Theorem, and supported numerous other research projects.” Also on Monday, AI startup Physical Superintelligence announced a new proof of the Aaronson‑Ambainis conjecture, a pivotal step in setting theoretical limits for quantum computing. Notably, the lab said the result was achieved by running “a non-public Anthropic model” within PSI’s own system. Anthropic did not confirm or deny whether Fable 5.2 was the model in question. sources.title: Anthropic lança Claude Mythos 5.2 e Fable 5.2, novas versões de sua IA ‘superpoderosa’
sources.text: A Anthropic lançou o Claude Mythos 5.2 nesta segunda-feira (9), sua mais nova versão de inteligência artificial de fronteira, apresentada como uma das mais poderosas da empresa. O novo modelo supera o Opus 5.5 em quase todos os testes sintéticos divulgados no anúncio, com resultados superiores em programação, pesquisa, cibersegurança e conhecimentos gerais. Para o público geral, ele chega sob a roupagem do Fable 5.2, com salvaguardas de segurança mais rigorosas. Os testadores dos novos Mythos 5.2 e Fable 5.2 destacam que os modelos conseguem se comunicar de forma mais clara do que as versões anteriores , gerando respostas até 30% mais rapidamente do que as respectivas edições 5.1. Na estreia, os novos modelos também estão disponíveis por um custo menor: US$ 8 (R$ 44,06) por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$ 40 (R$ 220) por milhão de tokens de saída. Além do modo convencional, as novas IAs também estão disponíveis no modo opcional “Fast” , que torna a geração de tokens 2,5 vezes mais rápida, mas pelo dobro do preço original. Por se tratar de modelos de fronteira, o Mythos e o Fable são mais apropriados para projetos elaborados e tarefas que demandam maior capacidade de raciocínio. A Anthropic ressalta que o Claude Opus 5.5 continua sendo a opção mais poderosa para uso cotidiano e orienta a escolha da IA de acordo com a complexidade da tarefa. Em um exemplo de demonstração de capacidade, a Anthropic usou o Fable 5.2 para desenvolver um protótipo de sistema operacional . O modelo coordenou 1.000 agentes menores ao longo de oito dias para escrever, testar e revisar o código. O resultado foi um SO funcional capaz de rodar num notebook, com núcleo e drivers próprios, suporte a gerenciamento de janelas e integração com o próprio Claude. “O Fable 5.2 também pode desempenhar o papel de Consultor, em que modelos como Haiku, Sonnet ou Opus o consultam para ajudar a resolver problemas mais complexos, ou Orquestrador, em que ele delega tarefas mais simples a modelos menores”, descreve a empresa. Nos testes sintéticos apresentados, o Fable 5.2 foi comparado com o Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra e o recente Gemini 4 Carbon . A nova IA da Anthropic supera os demais modelos na maioria dos testes apresentados, mas fica atrás do Opus 5.5 no teste de trabalho de conhecimento (AA-Briefcase v1.1). O Gemini 4 Carbon também sai vitorioso no teste de fluxos de trabalho empresariais (AutomationBench). Mais detalhes sobre a metodologia dos testes estão disponíveis no site da Anthropic. Segundo a Anthropic, mais de 90% das mudanças adicionadas à sua base de código são escritas pelo Claude sob supervisão humana. O Fable 5.2 foi utilizado para resolver bugs mais persistentes com maior agilidade, otimizar o desempenho dos serviços e concluir projetos de software de maior valor. O Mythos 5.2, por sua vez, é o modelo mais capaz para engenharia de cibersegurança, segundo a Anthropic. A empresa afirma que a IA consegue encontrar mais vulnerabilidades e apresenta melhor desempenho na reprodução e resolução de problemas. Assim como nas versões anteriores, o Claude Mythos 5.2 continua acessível exclusivamente para participantes do Cyber Verification Program e do Life Sciences Verification Program . Clientes do Claude Enterprise também podem consultar o modelo por meio do Claude Security. O Fable 5.2, por sua vez, está disponível para o público geral em todos os canais em que o Claude pode ser acessado , além das plataformas das provedoras Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud e Microsoft Azure. No Claude Platform, o modelo pode ser acionado pelo identificador claude-fable-5-2 . Quer ficar por dentro das novidades do mundo da tecnologia? sources.title: Anthropic launches Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 with science, coding upgrades
sources.text: Anthropic PBC today pulled back the curtains on Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, its two most capable large language models to date. The LLMs are identical as far as their core capabilities are concerned. The difference is that Fable 5.2 blocks certain biology and cybersecurity use cases, while Mythos 5.2 includes more relaxed guardrails. The latter model is only available to trusted researchers through a pair of limited-access programs. Anthropic tested Fable 5.2 against its predecessor across 14 artificial intelligence benchmarks. The model beat Fable 5.1’s score by more than 10% across most of the tests. It’s particularly adept at scientific research: Fable 5.2 scored 74.6% on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, a 22% improvement over Fable 5.1. Earlier this year, Anthropic used an unreleased LLM to generate a computer-verifiable version of a famous mathematical proof. The project took 11 days. According to Anthropic, Fable 5.2 reduced the workflow to 30 hours by spinning up 1,000 agents to parallelize calculations. In a separate project, it answered two open questions about a theoretical physics concept related to black holes. The company also tested Mythos 5.2, the invite-only version of Fable 5.2. It asked the model to study the protective shells of harmless viruses called AAVs. AAV shells, or capsids as they’re known in scientific parlance, are used by some therapies to deliver drugs. Mythos 5.2 accurately modeled the structure of 28 out of the 34 AAV capsids it studied. The result is notable because capsids comprise dozens of different proteins. Other cutting-edge models that are optimized for biology research, notably Google DeepMind’s AlphaFold2, can only model the structure of individual proteins. The creators of the latter model won one half of the 2024 Nobel Prize in chemistry. Fable 5.2 includes guardrails that block most research biology questions and many cybersecurity-related prompts. If users enter a request that falls into either of those categories, the model sends it to Opus 4.8 or Opus 5. Anthropic says Fable 5.2 is 55% less likely to erroneously block safe prompts than Fable 5.1. The model outperforms its predecessor by more than 13% across two coding benchmarks called FrontierCode 2.0 FrontierSWE 2.0. According to Anthropic, one of its engineers put the model’s programming capabilities to the test by asking it to build an operating system. Fable 5.2 spun up up 1,000 agents that completed the task in about eight days. The operating system they created can run on a laptop, offers network access and features a Claude sidebar. Anthropic sees customers using Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 to speed up highly complicated, open-ended technical tasks. The company says more day-to-day workflows can be automated more efficiently using Opus 5.5, an LLM it introduced in July. Users can also combine the models by having Opus 5.5 ask Fable 5.2 or Mythos 5.2 for advise when it encounters a bottleneck. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are priced at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. That makes them 20% more affordable than Anthropic’s previous-generation models. Both LLMs offer a high-performance mode that generates prompt responses 2.5 times faster than the standard tier for double the price. stories.title: Meet Jensen Huang’s son-in-law, a former pro skier and the Nvidia CEO’s ‘consigliere’ who could play a massive role in the company’s succession plan
stories.summary: Nvidia is now investigating Huang’s affair with a woman U.S. officials suspect of spying for China, raising concerns of a “key-man risk” of who could one day replace him.

sources.name: Fortune
sources.title: Meet Jensen Huang’s son-in-law, a former pro skier and the Nvidia CEO’s ‘consigliere’ who could play a massive role in the company’s succession plan
sources.text: In January, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was asked how he’s managed to lead the company since its 1993 founding. “The secret for being CEO for this long is, one, don’t get fired, and, two, don’t get bored,” he said at an event in Las Vegas. “I don’t know which one comes first. How long [will I continue as CEO]? For as long as I deserve it.” Ten months later, Huang is putting that adage to the test: Over the weekend, he admitted to having an affair with a business executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of acting as an operative for the Chinese government. China’s foreign ministry denied the allegation. As Huang faces increased scrutiny after he admitted to the affair with an alleged spy, he now faces questions about whether he can continue on as the company’s top brass. Nvidia has since launched an independent investigation into its CEO and his romantic relationship with suspected spy Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed International. Megaspeed is a data center and cloud computing company and one of Asia’s largest buyers of Nvidia chips. Nvidia’s board said Sunday that it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” Huang said in a statement on Sunday. “Today’s news will not slow Nvidia. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as CEO without interruption,” a company spokesperson told Fortune in a statement. The probe has reinvigorated investors’ concerns about the need to construct a succession plan, which, notably, Huang and Nvidia have not publicly shared. As of Monday morning, Nvidia stock is down more than 6%. Bernstein analysts, in a note published on Sunday, noted it would be unclear who could or would fill Huang’s shoes because the identity of his company is so inextricably linked to his own. “Nvidia is not an ordinary company and Jensen is not an ordinary CEO,” they wrote. “He IS Nvidia, clearly sets the long term strategy and direction, and (with supposedly 60 direct reports) pulls most of the company’s strings himself.” Huang’s two children, Madison and Spencer Huang, both have roles in the company, but Huang’s son-in-law Nico Caprez, Nvidia’s 35-year-old vice president of global AI infrastructure growth, could be among the next in line to lead the AI juggernaut. “I do imagine Huang is kind of preparing [Madison] and Nico for that next step,” one Nvidia employee who works with Caprez, told The Information last month. Caprez is a former alpine skier representing Switzerland who began his career as a Boston Consulting Group consultant. He graduated with an MBA from the London Business School in 2021, where he met Madison Huang. The two married this September. While Madison serves as a senior director of physical AI and robotics product marketing, and Spencer is a director of robotics product management, Caprez rose through the ranks at Nvidia to lead global AI infrastructure growth in less than three years, starting as a corporate development manager in February 2024 before becoming the director of global AI infrastructure enablement for Nvidia’s cloud partners about a year ago. The young executive was part of deal-making efforts to raise $500 billion with six major asset managers including Apollo Global Management and Blackstone , to finance Nvidia chips for data centers in August. Caprez also reportedly assisted in Nvidia’s efforts to take minority stakes in two data center developers as part of its AI infrastructure buildout. Senior leadership has extolled Caprez’s value both within the company and to the CEO more specifically. Vladimir Troy, Nvidia’s vice president of AI infrastructure who works alongside Caprez, said “Nico is very important.” A cloud executive who also met with Caprez called him “Jensen’s consigliere” in an interview with The Information. Huang, however, has been mum on who will lead the company in its next era, whenever that may be. In an interview with Bloomberg last month, the CEO shied away from speculation his daughter would one day replace him at Nvidia’s helm. “I don’t hope the job on her, and the reason for that is because if that’s their aspiration, Spencer of Madison’s, they have to go earn it, and it’s really, really hard work,” he said. “For many people, they can focus on their job and their families. When you’re the CEO of the company, you have to focus on, of course, your family. But I’ve got a whole bunch of other families I’m caring for. I’m responsible for an entire industry, and so I think the pressure of being the CEO is high.” To be sure, both Huang children are being well compensated. Madison received $1.23 million in total compensation for fiscal 2026, and Spencer received $1.32 million, according to Nvidia’s 2026 proxy statement . The filings clarify that these paydays are comparable to those of similar titles and responsibilities in the company, and that neither sibling shares a household with Huang, is an Nvidia executive officer, or reports directly to their father. Huang’s newly precarious spot at the top of his company has some worries not just about who one day replaces him, but whether anyone really can. “The so-called ‘key-man risk’ looms large here, and it’s doubtful markets have adequately priced it in,” economist Mohamed A. El-Erian wrote in a post on X . “This will not be easy for the board to navigate.” Daniel Newman, CEO of global technology research firm the Futurum Group, said that what’s made Huang so difficult to replace is that the company has been built around his leadership style, which leans autocratic. “He really drives everything that happens. He has a team of lieutenants that are in charge of making sure that what he asks becomes gospel, that it’s executed ferociously, maniacally,” Newman told Fortune . “The market has built such admiration and confidence for him that he’s become a Jobs or a Musk type of figure at Nvidia, where there just isn’t rea

sources.name: The Guardian Technology
sources.title: Jensen Huang’s image has been shattered. Could he be pushed out at Nvidia?
sources.text: Huang built Nvidia as a family business but after the co-founder had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, its board faces a difficult decision For more than 30 years, Jensen Huang has been the seemingly unshakable public face of Nvidia. He co-founded the company as a young engineer in 1993 and oversaw its growth into a multitrillion dollar chipmaker and bellwether of the AI industry at large. He’s also made it a family business. His children, Madison and Spencer, have taken leadership roles at the firm. While not a company executive, his wife, Lori Mills Huang, leads the family foundation which, as of 2024, controls over 60m Nvidia shares. But Huang’s image as a family man has been shattered as of Sunday. After the New York Times revealed at the end of October that Huang may have been targeted by a Chinese intelligence asset who he had developed a close relationship with, he admitted in a letter to employees on Sunday that he had been having an affair. Initially , Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said there was nothing out of the ordinary about Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang , an executive at a Singaporean datacenter firm, Megaspeed. US government officials had suspected Huang of smuggling American chips into China, prompting those officials to surveil and monitor her, the Times first reported. In the course of that surveillance, officials allegedly determined that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy and had gotten close with the Nvidia leader. Nvidia’s board of directors have now launched an independent investigation about the national security concerns surrounding Huang’s relationship. “I support the investigation and will cooperate fully,” Huang wrote in his letter. “I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.” Megaspeed did not respond to a Guardian request for comment before publication. In his letter, Huang apologized to his family, acknowledging how much they’ve supported him. His wife, Mills, kept a relatively low profile and didn’t play a formal role at Nvidia. However, in a 2023 interview with the New Yorker, Huang shared that Mills had also worked in Silicon Valley as a microchips engineer before stepping away to raise their children. “Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support,” Huang wrote in his letter to employees. “They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it.” Both his children now hold high ranking roles at the company, despite not initially pursuing careers in tech. His daughter, Madison, serves as the senior director of product and technical marketing for physical AI platforms, but got her start as a chef. She attended the Culinary Institute of America and Le Cordon Bleu before going to business school and transitioning to luxury marketing. She previously worked at LVMH – the parent company of Lous Vuitton. Spencer , for his part, now serves as the director of product for Robotics at Nvidia but spent much of his career as a consultant before joining his father’s company as a product manager. Before consulting, he owned and co-founded a craft cocktail bar in Taiwan. In his letter, Huang reiterated his commitment to Nvidia, saying he hoped to earn back his colleagues’ and employees’ trust. However, analysts and investors say there’s a chance he may be removed as CEO after the board’s investigation. “This is a black eye moment for Jensen and will spark multiple congressional inquiries at a minimum and will create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons,” said Dan Ives, a partner and analyst at investment bank Yorkville Ives. “There is clearly risk as discussed that Jensen could be removed as CEO depending on the board investigation and this will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally.” Ives said the family’s role at Nvidia adds some complexities for the board. “The board has to make its decision independent of the family spider web of Jensen and his family at Nvidia,” Ives told the Guardian. “It makes this a very complex situation for the board to navigate with the world watching.” Huang is to Nvidia what Steve Jobs was to Apple, said Ken Mahoney, the CEO and president of Mahoney Asset Management. “If you asked any Nvidia investor or anyone involved in tech and markets, would they like to see Jensen gone? Definitely not, but [Nvidia] would survive,” Mahoney said. “Losing Huang would introduce a lot of uncertainty, particularly given his influence over Nvidia’s strategy, culture, and relationships with major technology companies,” he continued. “The bigger question is whether a successor could maintain Huang’s strategic vision and ability to anticipate where the industry is heading, and how that new leader could be tested along the way if things become difficult.” Executive affairs or inappropriate relationships have recently unseated CEOs, according to executive recruiting and coaching firm Challenger Gray and Christmas. In 2024, the CEO of Astronomer was caught on a kiss cam with the company’s chief people officer, leading him to resign shortly after. Nestlé fired CEO Laurent Freixe for a relationship with a subordinate. Nvidia offers a more complex picture. On one hand, Huang’s affair is not just a matter morals or ethics, there are potential national security concerns. On the other, Huang is core to the DNA of Nvidia which in turn is the bedrock of the entire AI industry – an industry upon which the economy relies greatly. sources.text: The Nvidia CEO has been in a unique position to to influence AI export controls.﻿ The Nvidia CEO has been in a unique position to to influence AI export controls.﻿ It’s difficult to overstate Nvidia’s power in today’s AI landscape. The company’s chips are the bedrock upon which advanced AI technology in the US is being built, and demand has consistently outpaced supply for years. Nvidia has also been an influential investor in a wide range of up-and-coming AI companies in recent years, with about $99 billion worth of equity investments in frontier AI labs, neoclouds, infrastructure companies, and more. Its chief executive has even become close with President Donald Trump. This is why, as both cofounder and longtime CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang would be a valuable target for a foreign adversary with sights on the American AI industry. Huang is in hot water after news broke of his extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen) is an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud provider and a top Nvidia customer. Questions are swirling around how the affair may have influenced Huang’s reported push to sell advanced chips to China — and potentially even influenced President Trump’s own decisions surrounding AI export controls. Jensen Huang would be a valuable target for a foreign adversary with sights on the American AI industry US officials believe the Megaspeed executive is a foreign intelligence asset that has funneled information straight to the Chinese government, per The New York Times — in particular, officials reportedly believe that Megaspeed is related to a convoluted web of Chinese companies working together to access chips in bulk and perhaps even illegally get some of those chips into China. Alibaba is reportedly one of Megaspeed’s top customers. “It’s not entirely surprising that the CEO of arguably one of the most important, if not the most important, AI chip companies is the target of some sort of intelligence-gathering from countries like China,” Hanna Dohmen, a senior research analyst at CSET, said in an interview with The Verge , adding that an alleged spy would potentially be interested in “better understanding what the US government is thinking on export controls,” as well as gathering information on Huang’s conversations with the Trump administration, attempting to influence policy, and gathering information on trade secrets like “who’s buying Nvidia’s chips, who’s getting them first, what’s coming next in terms of AI chips.” Megaspeed’s sister company, headquartered in Malaysia, spent $4.8 billion or more on Nvidia chips and technology between June 2024 and February 2026, the Times reported, citing trade records from trade platform ImportGenius. The transaction sizes were outside the norm for a small company, particularly when Nvidia chips are so difficult to get. ”Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job” Nvidia spokespeople had said Huang’s relationship with the Megaspeed executive was strictly business. Their interactions were described as “not unusual or unexpected” in statements to the press. Nvidia’s line was, “Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job.” But at some point, their relationship became personal. In June 2024, just before Megaspeed became an Nvidia customer, photos show the two with other AI executives at a bar in Taipei after a local trade show; the following year, they reportedly had a business dinner in Taipei with others as well. But in private, according to US officials cited by the Times , the two’s relationship raised alarm bells for the US government — they had reportedly been surveilling the Megaspeed executive for months, if not longer, and that’s how it came out that she was in close contact with Huang. The revelation is particularly concerning because of Huang’s lobbying role. He’d been trying to convince the Trump administration and Congress to loosen export controls for sending advanced semiconductors to China, ostensibly so that Nvidia could sell more chips. We now know this was happening around the same time that Huang was spotted at the Taiwan dinner with Alice Huang in May 2025, according to Culper Research , which shorted Nvidia’s stock earlier this year. That dinner occurred shortly after Nvidia had shared the Trump administration’s new restrictions on its China-specific H20 chips in April. Just a couple months after the Taiwan dinner, Huang reportedly met with Trump in the Oval Office in July 2025 to plead his case for loosening export restrictions on Nvidia’s advanced semiconductors. Days later, the company announced that the administration had blessed sales of its H20 chips to China. Huang had argued that spreading American chips to China would help establish US technology as the standard, rather than allowing for Chinese chips to grow, according to The New York Times . After setbacks earlier in the second Trump term in export policy to China, Huang began speaking with then-White House AI czar David Sacks in 2025, who became the key advocate for Nvidia’s view that selling American chips to China would be beneficial, the Times reported. By October 2025, Huang was lobbying Trump to allow Nvidia to sell more advanced chips to China, ahead of Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, per the Times ; but after Trump considered the proposal , he ultimately decided not to move forward. (That same month, Huang hired an external PR firm known for handling sex scandals, Wired reported.) The same rules would apply to other US chipmakers, he wrote on Truth Social at the time. “It is in Nvidia’s interest and in Jensen Huang’s interest to lobby for looser export control restrictions” CSET’s Dohmen said that during the past two years, the US has seen a light loosening of AI

sources.title: Trump stands by Nvidia boss Jensen Huang despite spy scandal, but FBI is investigating
sources.text: The revelations this weekend that Nvidia Corp. boss Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair with a woman who has been accused of working for Chinese intelligence have now ensnared U.S. President Donald Trump, raising further questions about national security. At the same time, the Federal Bureau of Investigation said it’s looking into the affair, meaning it’s likely to get continuing attention in coming weeks or longer. Nvidia said it has launched an investigation into Chief Executive Huang’s actions after he admitted to cheating on his wife with a woman known as Alice Huang (no relation), who serves as the CEO of a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed . U.S. intelligence officials suspect Alice Huang has been feeding information about Huang and the chipmaker’s plans to the Chinese government. And though Trump was informed of the possible infiltration, he has continued working with Nvidia and Huang on domestic policy issues related to technology and artificial intelligence, which have become of vital importance to the U.S. economy. Huang has spent the last two years cultivating a close relationship with Trump, gaining extraordinary access to America’s top decision-maker and influence over the country’s AI strategy. He has gone from being virtually unknown to the president to being a key member of a cadre of technology industry executives accompanying him on trips aboard Air Force One, including a visit to China in May. He has come to be seen as a major ally of Trump, attending numerous White House events while repeatedly praising his policies. Notably, his company made a $25 million donation to the president’s gaudy ballroom project, becoming its top corporate contributor alongside Apple Inc. Those efforts seem to have gone a long way toward getting Huang into the president’s good graces, and it seems to have paid off for the company. Last year, after months of lobbying from Huang and Nvidia, the Trump administration agreed that it could sell more advanced chips to China that were previously banned from being exported to the country. Though that decision was widely known, it seems that the Trump administration has intervened in other ways to protect Nvidia’s interests. Earlier today, the New York Times reported that a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed, which was suspected of smuggling banned chips into China, was abruptly canceled after receiving an email from Nvidia’s general counsel. Commerce official Jeff Kessler, who was nominated for the role by Trump, reportedly gave Nvidia permission to contact the investigation team and mention his name, which goes against standard protocol. Investigators had grown suspicious that Megaspeed was essentially just a front for smuggling embargoed Nvidia chips into China, but the correspondence from Nvidia’s general counsel Tim Teter kicked off a kerfuffle that ultimately led to the investigation being transferred to the Department of Justice. But Trump defended Huang late on Sunday, stating that the Nvidia boss is an “honorable guy” who has not committed any wrongdoing. The president had been briefed about the suspected Chinese intelligence operation as far back as October 2025, but decided not to do anything , according to the Times. “I haven’t heard that he’s done anything wrong,” Trump said. “He dealt with somebody, but, you know, so does everybody else.” Trump continued to defend Huang on Monday when quizzed about the situation again, before revealing that the Federal Bureau of Investigation is also looking into his relationship with the suspected spy. “I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he’ll be in good shape,” he said at a White House briefing. Despite the apparent protection afforded by Trump, Huang appears to be taking no chances. A report in Wired said today that the Nvidia boss has hired the services of a public relations firm called Heller that specializes in handling public scandals. Rise Heller, the firm’s founder, has developed a reputation for helping powerful men sidestep allegations of sexual misconduct and other personal controversies. She previously represented clients including the former Congressman Anthony Weiner, the writer Jeffrey Toobin and the chef Mario Batali, Wired reported. Tech industry personalities have also leapt to Huang’s defense. Shaun Maguire, a partner at the venture capital firm Sequoia Capital said in a post on X that Huang is “one of the greatest entrepreneurs of this generation,” and stressed that although he did something “incredibly dumb,” he believes there was “no bad intention.” Tesla Inc. CEO Elon Musk later shared Maguire’s post, saying he agrees with all of it. However, no intervention has managed to protect Nvidia’s stock, which slid more than 4% on Monday , wiping around $190 billion off of the company’s valuation. Nvidia is scheduled to hold its next financial earnings call on Nov. 17, in which Huang is likely to face some very difficult questions — if he is on the call as has been customary. sources.name: Canaltech
sources.title: Google lança novos chips de IA para aumentar segurança e poder computacional
sources.text: Por André Lourenti Magalhães • Editado por Jones Oliveira | 09/11/2026 às 10:00 O Google Cloud anunciou dois novos TPUs para a infraestrutura de IA nesta segunda-feira (09). De olho nos impactos dos agentes de IA no uso computacional, a empresa traz soluções para aumentar a segurança de dados e permitir janelas de contexto massivas. O TPU 8tx tem o objetivo de trazer inferências mais seguras e segurança computacional a nível de hardware. O chip é ideal para empresas que precisam tratar e treinar dados confidenciais e conta com hosts CPU personalizados da AMD para garantir que as informações sejam armazenadas com segurança. Já o TPU 8i Max foi criado para acabar com possíveis gargalos de memória no processamento de IA e permitir trabalhos em larga escala . O chip tem suporte a janelas de contexto massivas, aumenta a largura de banda da memória para transmissão de dados e permite maior densidade computacional (maior poder de computação por metro quadrado e por watt). Os novos componentes ampliam a linha de TPUs do Google: a linha de 8ª geração foi anunciada em abril deste ano com os modelos TPU 8i e TPU 8t . O Google informa que o aumento do uso de agentes de IA foi um dos fatores para a criação de novos chips. O salto da escala humana para a escala agêntica exige maior poder computacional, especialmente pelo fato de que um bot pode criar fluxos de trabalho complexos e contínuos. “Com a computação migrando da escala humana para a escala de agentes, as empresas estão pedindo aceleradores que possam raciocinar sobre as massivas janelas de contexto dos modelos de IA. Além disso, alguns clientes, altamente regulamentados, estão pedindo recursos de criptografia especializados para cargas de trabalho únicas”, explica o Diretor de Tecnologia e Vice-Presidente Sênior de IA e Infraestrutura do Google, Amin Vahdat. Sigla para Tensor Processing Unit (“Unidade de processamento de tensor”, em tradução livre), TPU é um chip desenvolvido pelo Google para uso em aprendizado de máquina e infraestrutura de IA . O componente é usado em data centers e permite maior poder de computação para inferência no treinamento de modelos .

sources.title: Google lança novos TPUs para otimizar tarefas de agentes de IA e melhorar segurança
sources.text: O Google anunciou nesta segunda-feira (9) o TPU 8i Max e o TPU 8tx , dois novos chips de inteligência artificial (IA) destinados ao aprimoramento de tarefas realizadas por agentes autônomos em meio à ampla implementação desses sistemas no setor produtivo. As novidades se juntam às outras duas configurações de 8ª geração lançadas este ano . “Com a computação migrando da escala humana para a escala de agentes, as empresas estão pedindo aceleradores que possam raciocinar sobre as massivas janelas de contexto dos modelos de IA. Além disso, alguns clientes, altamente regulamentados, estão pedindo recursos de criptografia especializados para cargas de trabalho únicas”, afirmou Amin Vahdat, Diretor de Tecnologia e Vice-Presidente Sênior de IA e Infraestrutura do Google, em comunicado. Integrando a segurança diretamente na camada de hardware, o TPU 8tx mantém dados sensíveis e pesos de modelos protegidos e isolados mesmo durante o uso ativo , de acordo com a companhia. Além disso, apresenta latência duas vezes menor na comparação com a versão 8t anunciada em abril. Já o TPU 8i Max foi projetado para lidar com eventuais gargalos de memória que podem surgir ao executar dezenas de agentes de uma só vez. Ele disponibiliza o dobro de poder computacional, de SRAM e da largura de banda de HBM do TPU 8i, trazendo fluidez para grandes cargas de trabalho. A novidade também acomoda o dobro de silício dentro da mesma estrutura, permitindo que data centers implantem significativamente mais poder de computação por metro quadrado e por watt, como explicou a big tech. A Unidade de Processamento Tensorial (TPU) é utilizada de diferentes maneiras pela gigante das buscas. A tecnologia aprimora o treinamento de modelos próprios da companhia para cargas de trabalho de agentes , por exemplo, disponibilizando-os para clientes do Google Cloud . Usuários da infraestrutura em nuvem também podem implantar os TPUs em seus data centers, diante do aumento da demanda. São quase 100 clientes utilizando a tecnologia, segundo o Google, incluindo laboratórios de ponta, universidades, varejistas e empresas de negociação, entre outros. stories.title: Escándalo en Nvidia: el consejo investiga a su CEO tras confesar una infidelidad en un caso de espionaje
stories.summary: El CEO de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, ha admitido una infidelidad en pleno escrutinio por una presunta operación de inteligencia e IA vinculada a una exdirectiva de Megaspeed.

sources.name: Computer Hoy
sources.title: Escándalo en Nvidia: el consejo investiga a su CEO tras confesar una infidelidad en un caso de espionaje
sources.text: Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google. El CEO de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, ha admitido una infidelidad en pleno escrutinio por una presunta operación de inteligencia e IA vinculada a una exdirectiva de Megaspeed. El líder en tarjetas gráficas ha dado un ultimátum al afirmar que "el PC ha muerto" debido a que ahora los dispositivos se están convirtiendo en agentes personales , pero eso no es lo único en lo que se ha enfocado el CEO de Nvidia, porque sus opiniones han estado alrededor de que uno de los países se está quedando atrás en tecnología , pero lo que no se sabía hasta ahora es que Jensen Huang haría una confesión personal inédita al estar bajo una investigación relacionada con posibles actividades de espionaje vinculadas a China . La situación ha escalado hasta el punto de que el consejo de administración ha puesto en marcha un caso independiente para determinar si existió algún riesgo para la compañía o para información de carácter sensible . De hecho, las sospechas giran en torno a una exdirectiva de Megaspeed, empresa que compra hardware de Nvidia para centros de datos, y a supuestos informes de inteligencia que la vincularían con organismos estatales chinos. Aunque las acusaciones no han sido demostradas públicamente y Nvidia insiste en que no tiene evidencias de que se hayan comprometido secretos empresariales. ¿Es esta una situación crítica en la carrera global de la inteligencia artificial? Todo apunta a que podría ser un problema similar al de Apple y OpenAI por robar secretos comerciales para desarrollar un dispositivo de IA . El máximo responsable de la empresa líder en chips para inteligencia artificial ha llamado la atención de toda la industria, principalmente por un mensaje en el que se destaca que p odría haber filtrado información confidencial de la compañía hacia entes externos y ajenos. Todo ha comenzado tras una publicación donde se revelan datos en donde Jensen Huang parece estar relacionándose con Alice Huang , una exdirectiva de Megaspeed señalada en diversos reportes periodísticos por presuntos vínculos con estructuras de inteligencia chinas. El CEO de Nvidia decidió emitir un comunicado en el que admite haber sido infiel a su esposa, diciendo textualmente que "fui infiel a mi esposa. Mis actos le hicieron daño a ella y a nuestros hijos". También reconoce que ha decepcionado a su familia, a los trabajadores y a los accionistas de la empresa. ¿Por qué una ruptura amorosa supone el peligro de toda una empresa? Al estar en una posición tan elevada y formar parte de una de las compañías más importantes de la industria tecnológica, hay información confidencial de por medio que está en juego. Cualquier decisión o acción que provengas de parte del CEO, seguro que influye de diversas formas en toda la ruta futura del equipo . En este caso se debe a que una persona tan cercana como la esposa puede actuar por impulso y revelar detalles que se consideran secreto. Según la compañía, el consejo de administración ha iniciado una investigación supervisada por consejeros independientes y expertos jurídicos externos para analizar toda la información disponible. Aun así, el acontecimiento convierte cualquier sospecha en un asunto de enorme relevancia debido al papel dominante que ocupa Nvidia en el mercado de aceleradores para inteligencia artificial. La cuestión adquiere todavía más relevancia porque la empresa se encuentra en medio de la disputa tecnológica entre Washington y Pekín. Los procesadores de Nvidia son fundamentales para entrenar modelos avanzados de IA y Estados Unidos mantiene estrictas restricciones sobre la exportación de determinadas soluciones de alto rendimiento a China. Megaspeed ya se encontraba bajo observación por parte de autoridades estadounidenses debido a preguntas sobre el destino final de algunos chips avanzados utilizados en infraestructuras de inteligencia artificial. Nvidia ha defendido públicamente que cumple las normativas vigentes y que realiza verificaciones para garantizar que sus productos llegan a los compradores autorizados , pero el caso ha reactivado el debate sobre la eficacia de los controles tecnológicos en una industria cada vez más estratégica. La repercusión política tampoco ha tardado en llegar. Varios presidentes de comisiones del Congreso estadounidense han solicitado una reunión informativa a puerta cerrada con Huang para conocer con mayor detalle la situación. Por ahora, Nvidia mantiene su respaldo a Jensen Huang y ha confirmado que continuará al frente de la compañía durante el desarrollo de la investigación. La empresa insiste en que colaborará con cualquier revisión necesaria y que la prioridad es esclarecer los hechos.

sources.title: El escándalo de espionaje que rodea al CEO de Nvidia acaba de dar otro giro: Trump dice que el FBI ya lo investiga
sources.text: Donald Trump ha situado al FBI en el centro del escándalo que afecta a Jensen Huang, consejero delegado de Nvidia. El presidente estadounidense afirmó el lunes 9 de noviembre que la agencia federal estaba investigando el asunto , después de que trascendieran sospechas sobre una posible operación de espionaje chino relacionada con una mujer con la que el directivo mantuvo una relación extramatrimonial. Trump aseguró que había hablado personalmente con él y que este le había dicho que desconocía los supuestos vínculos de la mujer con los servicios de inteligencia chinos. Sin embargo, el mandatario no detalló el alcance de las pesquisas. Para entender cómo se ha llegado hasta aquí, hay que retroceder al domingo 8 de noviembre. Como ya contamos en Xataka , Huang publicó un mensaje en la web de Nvidia en el que reconocía haber sido infiel a su esposa, pedía disculpas a su familia y a la compañía y se comprometía a colaborar con las pesquisas. Ese mismo día, el consejo de administración anunció una investigación independiente para esclarecer si su máximo responsable había sido objetivo de una operación de inteligencia extranjera. La empresa afirmó que no tenía motivos para creer que se hubieran comprometido secretos corporativos o la seguridad nacional estadounidense. Detrás de estas sospechas aparece el nombre de Alice Huang, antigua directiva de Megaspeed International, una empresa singapurense de centros de datos que compra chips a Nvidia. Según publicó Financial Times , un memorando elaborado por funcionarios estadounidenses a partir de información de inteligencia la vinculaba con el Ministerio de Seguridad del Estado chino, que supuestamente la habría reclutado para obtener información sobre el ejecutivo. No obstante, el documento no se ha hecho público y las acusaciones no han sido demostradas. Por su parte, el Gobierno de Singapur aclaró que no había investigado a Alice Huang por sus presuntos vínculos con Pekín, aunque confirmó que seguían abiertas las pesquisas sobre Megaspeed. El interés del caso va mucho más allá de la vida privada de un directivo. No es ningún secreto que Nvidia ocupa una posición central en el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial gracias a sus chips, una tecnología cuyo acceso Estados Unidos intenta controlar mediante restricciones a las exportaciones hacia China. Huang ha realizado gestiones ante Washington para flexibilizar esas limitaciones y conseguir permisos para comercializar modelos como el H200 , un procesador avanzado que no figura entre los más recientes de la compañía. Según documentación presentada por Nvidia ante la SEC , el Gobierno estadounidense autorizó ventas limitadas de este modelo a determinados clientes chinos, aunque Pekín también ha impuesto restricciones a su comercialización. La controversia también ha provocado respuestas oficiales a ambos lados del Pacífico. El portavoz del Ministerio de Exteriores chino, Guo Jiakun, rechazó las acusaciones de espionaje , que calificó de infundadas y de intentos de desacreditar a China . Mientras tanto, en Estados Unidos, los presidentes de tres comités de la Cámara de Representantes habían solicitado días antes una sesión informativa a puerta cerrada con Huang para el 18 de noviembre. Su objetivo es conocer los contactos del ejecutivo con Alice Huang y las medidas de Nvidia frente al espionaje extranjero. Se trata de una petición parlamentaria, no de una determinación de culpabilidad. Mientras todo esto se desarrolla, as acciones de Nvidia cayeron un 4,3% al cierre del lunes 9 de noviembre, lo que redujo su capitalización bursátil en unos 190.000 millones de dólares, según Reuters. Apenas cinco minutos después del cierre del mercado, se presentó una demanda contra la empresa y su consejero delegado , impulsada por accionistas que buscan tramitarla como acción colectiva y que los acusan de haber ocultado información relevante. Mientras avanzan las investigaciones, sigue sin estar claro si hubo acceso a información sensible y qué consecuencias podría tener todo esto para el futuro de la compañía.
